caption: Studies are ordered with the 6 cohorts whose enrolled population was confined to psoriasis or psoriatic arthritis first (Bakkour 2016, Fabiano 2014, Day 2023, Kawakami 2016, Koga 2025, Kunimi 2018), followed by the 6 mixed-diagnosis cohorts (Berthold 2013, Nguyen 2021, George 2017, Di Martino 2023, Vasavada 2023, Borgas 2020). Diagnosis confined to psoriasis or PsA and psoriasis or PsA outcomes separable are two different questions and are reported as two separate columns. They diverge for exactly 2 studies: Day 2023 was confined to psoriasis but its outcomes are not separable to PsA, and Borgas 2020 was not confined to psoriasis or PsA but does report partially separable PsA outcomes. Counts are patients unless procedures, surgeries, or cases are specified. Directness follows the primary comparison: Direct denotes actual continuation versus planned interruption of the same therapy, Timing-proxy denotes a shorter versus longer interval from last dose to surgery, and Contextual denotes biologic users versus nonusers or a chronic-use classification; timing-proxy and contextual studies were treated as indirect. TNF inhibitors were present in all 12 studies and were the only class with cohort-level isolable data, whereas interleukin-12/23 and JAK inhibitors appeared only inside mixed or aggregate exposures, and no study contributed interleukin-17, interleukin-23, or tyrosine kinase 2 inhibitor data. Berthold 2013 and Borgas 2020 share an overlapping Lund and Skane arthroplasty population and never enter the same pool, under the pre-specified overlap rule. Across the 4 studies in the primary comparative pool, 352 of the 1,979 analysis units (17.8%) carried a recorded diagnosis of psoriasis or psoriatic arthritis (Bakkour 77, Fabiano 131, Nguyen 77, Berthold 67); this describes cohort composition only, because in Berthold 2013 and Nguyen 2021 these patients appear in a baseline diagnosis table and their outcomes are not reported separately. The psoriasis- or PsA-specific evidence remains the 208 analysis units (10.5%) contributed by the 2 cohorts composed entirely of patients with psoriasis or PsA, Bakkour 2016 and Fabiano 2014. Full study characteristics are given in Table S1, the evidence-classification matrix in Table S2, and outcome event data in Table S3.
abbreviations: Abbreviations: bDMARD, biologic disease-modifying antirheumatic drug; CDC, Centers for Disease Control and Prevention; csDMARD, conventional synthetic disease-modifying antirheumatic drug; DAPSA, Disease Activity in Psoriatic Arthritis; JAK, Janus kinase; MA1, primary comparative pool for infection or wound complications; MA2, comparative disease-flare pool; PJI, periprosthetic joint infection; PsA, psoriatic arthritis; RIPO, Registro dell'Implantologia Protesica Ortopedica; SSI, surgical-site infection; TNF, tumor necrosis factor; tsDMARD, targeted synthetic disease-modifying antirheumatic drug.

footnotes.text: Koga 2025: adalimumab was held for 2 weeks before surgery. This is a single dosing interval and a short guideline-concordant hold rather than uninterrupted continuation.

Nguyen 2021: the 2 psoriasis figures use different denominators. Psoriasis accounted for 27.2% of the 827-patient biologic cohort and for 45 of the 218 surgical procedures that enter the pooled analysis.

George 2017: only the infliximab-within-4-weeks stop-timing bin (1,162 surgeries) enters the pooled proportions, as a continuer proxy. The 8-to-12-week reference arm (747 surgeries) does not enter any pool.
Vasavada 2023: the 2 PsA figures use different denominators. PsA numbered 119 across the 428-patient matched cohort and about 50 within the 214 immunosuppression arms that form the flare pool.
